questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was really important to me that I would feel safe at my destination at all times, and that there would be a lot of different museums, events and other activities taking place in the city and the areas around it. Besides that it was also important for my choice that the university had a big selection of courses I found interesting. I therefore looked at the course list in advance and chose an english speaking university to allow me to choose between all the courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The university send a many emails with information before I arrived, and I got a person I could contact before arrival. She also hosted a meeting upon arrival and she was available throughout the entire semester if we needed help. There were also a lot of staff walking around campus the first couple of weeks who could help solve any kind of problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance when I arrived other than going to the science exchange student information meeting hosted by my contact person.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found our apartment through the facebook page called McGill Off-campus Housing. If you keep an eye out and reach out to the landlords fast this is a really good way to find an apartment. It is however important to note that many people are looking for an apartment so you have to check regularly. Furthermore it can be a good idea to look at the area before signing the contract to make sure that the distance to university or the nearest metrostation is acceptable. I believe that this group is rather safe, but it is always important to be aware of the chance of being tricked.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Generally speaking it is cheaper to live off campus and in this way you are not required to pay for the meal plan. The area around McGill is called the McGill ghetto as a lot of students live and have their daily life here, and living off campus is a nice way to use other areas of the city more.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an email from my host institution upon admission with a link to a website where I had to fill in the necessary information. During this registration process I got acces to my McGill email and website called minerva. Minerva was where the course registation took place, and after deciding which courses i wanted to take I could enter their numbers on the registration page at minerva once the registration opened.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to get help by sending an email to the contact person or the professor if a course for instance required special admission.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting 3 of the courses i originally wanted and the last course I was able to register for was really similar to the one i originally wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The course registration for exchange student opens after some other students have already registered meaning that some courses are already full or nearly full. And as all exchange students are able to register at the same time it might be hard to get the courses you want in the beginning. A lot of people are however dropping their courses again both before and during the add/drop period so it is important to keep an eye out as spots might become available. The professors are often really kind as well so if you experience any kind of problem you can try to send the professor an email.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one 200 level course, two 300 level courses and one 500 level course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My experience were that the professors at McGill focused less on methods compared to UCPH and instead of knowing how things work and how we know this we had to learn and remember a lot of details of the different subjects. They test you through quizzes and assignments throughout the entire semester which I found a little stressfull, but i eventually got used to it, and this made the exam period much easier. I only had one course with assigned reading for every lecture, and in general i found it easier to get a good result at McGill than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
QCST 200 - Intro to the Study of Quebec
PSYC 311 - Human Cognition and the Brain
MIMM 324 - Fundamental Virology
PHGY 518 - Artificial Cells

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It was really satisfied with all my courses, but I would especially recommend QCST 200 as I found it really interesting to learn more about the area I was living in. The course covers the history, the culture and todays issues of Quebec and the professor is great. She had guest lectures coming to class for nearly all lectures and it was always really interesting and a nice way to learn if you want to try something different from you normal field.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really encounter any unexpected costs. But I only had to pay for one book which was less than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think the prices were really similar to the danish prices. The prize was distributed differently on items in the supermarket than in Denmark, but the final price on all my groceries would be quite similar to what I would pay in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
McGill has a lot of different clubs for students to join. I were a part of the McGill outdoor club and I also attended events made by the Mafia club (they play the game called mafia or werewolf), chocolate club and the knitting club. I were also a part of a soccer intramural team, where we got to play against other McGill teams. 
No matter you interest it is possible to find a club, and it was a great way to get to know other people, and we often went to a bar or planned to meet another time after the meetings and events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend joining the outdoor club as you can join different trips throughout the semester and experience the nature around Montreal. They also have a frosh event before the semester starts where I went on a canoeing trip for three days in a national park.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend just walking around the different neighborhoods of Montreal and try all the cafes, museum and events that you find. You should also follow the website MTLblog as they post weekly updates of things to do in Montreal the following week.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture isn't much different from the danish culture, so it was really easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs or sport teams as this is an easier setting to socialize with local students than in classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging. If I should mention one thing it would be the fact that Quebec is a French speaking province meaning that messages in the metro for instance is only done in French, but it never caused me any problems even though I wasn't able to understand it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that the Canadians are so friendly and open. It is really easy to start a conversation with them.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be stressed by all the deadlines. They aren't that strict when marking your assignments and it is important to have freetime to experience the city. 
Join all the events at university that you find interesting. People are always happy to talk and it's a great way to make new friends if you show up alone. 
If you are going to use the metro often you can save a lot of money by showing up at the STM office at Berri UQAM

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: McGill has an interactive map you can find on the internet to show you the easiest ways to navigate between buildings at campus

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the most rewarding part was experiencing how I was able to build an everyday life and make new friends in a foreign country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was accepting that things take time and that it was hard to make friends, understand all the new systems and keeping up with the deadlines in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Montreal is an amazing city and McGill is a great university. Things can seem hard or overwhelming but it was one of the best experiences I have ever had, and everything will eventually be solved so it is important to have fun and enjoy the stay before it is time to go home as 4 months go by so fast.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
